command: RNX2CRX.exe < in.rnx > out.crx   (in.rnx = the corpus file decoded by rinexcore.io.hatanaka.crx_to_rnx, or a plain corpus file after rinexcore.io.compress.unwrap; stdin/stdout in binary mode on our side)
platform: Windows 11 x64; the mingw build writes stdout in text mode, so each LF is written as CRLF; the digests are of the output with CRLF -> LF

fields.rinex_sha256: sha256 of the RINEX bytes fed to stdin
fields.exit_code: RNX2CRX exit code (0 ok, 1 error, 2 warning)
fields.sha256_lf: sha256 of RNX2CRX's output, CRLF -> LF
fields.sha256_body: sha256 of that output without line 2 (CRINEX PROG / DATE, which holds the run date), so that a laptop without the exe can check our encoder's output against it
fields.lone_cr: CR bytes not followed by LF (0: the CRLF -> LF mapping is exact)
fields.ours: rnx_to_crx(r) against RNX2CRX(r), ignoring line 2 (CRINEX PROG / DATE): 'identical', 'identical-after-line-2' or 'differs@...'; 'refused: ...' where our encoder refuses
fields.decodes_back: our decoder on RNX2CRX's output gives r (CRX files) or crx_to_rnx(rnx_to_crx(r)) (plain files)
